newsitem.title: JAPAN: No plan to amend Japan 97/98 draft budget - MOF.
newsitem.headline: No plan to amend Japan 97/98 draft budget - MOF.

text.p: The Japanese government does not intend to accept any amendments to its draft budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Friday.

Asked whether the government has any plans to accept calls by the opposition to make amendments to the draft budget, Mitsuzuka said: "The draft has been looked over carefully and the cabinet has no intention of changing it."
He also said the government has still not made up its mind on whether to cut spending through changes during the implementation stage.
Mitsuzuka also said the government will conduct further discussions on fiscal reform so that it will be able to lay a framework for the 1998/99 budget by the end of the current parliamentary session.

He said he had directed ministry officials to start looking into ways to cut spending so that the Finance Ministry will be able to come up with a draft budget for 1998/99 soon after an outline has been drawn up.
Mitsuzuka said the ministry will do its utmost to submit a bill in the current parliamentary session to reform the finance ministry.
He added that if the reforms of the finance ministry are carried out they will lead to stable international financial markets.
